Achshaph
AK-shaf
proper noun
Hebrew Akshaph, perhaps “sorcery” or “enchantment,” a royal city in the border of Asher.

📖 Biblical Definition

Achshaph was a royal Canaanite city in the north, lying within the borders of the tribe of Asher. Its king answered the summons of Jabin king of Hazor and joined the great confederacy of northern kings who gathered at the waters of Merom to fight against Israel (Josh 11:1). When the LORD delivered that host into Israel’s hand, the king of Achshaph was slain among the rest, and his name is written in the roll of the thirty-one kings overthrown in the conquest (Josh 12:20). The city is afterward named among the bounds of Asher’s inheritance (Josh 19:25). The meaning of its name, bound up with sorcery or enchantment, fits the dark religion of the Canaanites, whose abominations of divination and witchcraft were among the reasons the LORD cast them out before Israel (Deut 18:9–12). Achshaph thus appears as one more heathen stronghold given over to judgment, its enchantments powerless against the word of the living God. It teaches that the spells and divinations of the nations cannot turn aside the purpose of the LORD, who gave the land to the seed of Abraham according to His oath.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A royal Canaanite city in Asher’s border whose king joined Jabin’s league; its name suggests sorcery.

ACHSHAPH, a royal Canaanite city in the north, within the bounds of Asher.

Its king was summoned by Jabin of Hazor to the northern confederacy (Josh 11:1).

He was slain when the LORD overthrew the league at Merom (Josh 11:8).

His name stands in the roll of the thirty-one kings (Josh 12:20).

The city is named among the borders of Asher (Josh 19:25).

📖 Key Scripture

Josh 11:1 — "And it came to pass, when Jabin king of Hazor had heard those things, that he sent to Jobab king of Madon, and to the king of Shimron, and to the king of Achshaph,"

Josh 12:20 — "The king of Shimronmeron, one; the king of Achshaph, one;"

Josh 19:25 — "And their border was Helkath, and Hali, and Beten, and Achshaph,"

Deut 18:10 — "There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,"

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place-name, not a doctrine in dispute; its lesson is that the enchantments of the heathen cannot turn aside the purpose of God.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that the sorceries woven into the name of Achshaph, like all the divinations of Canaan, were powerless against the LORD. He cast out the nations for their witchcraft and gave their land to His people; no enchantment could shield the city from the judgment that the abominations of the Amorite had ripened to receive.

Achshaph reminds the reader that the conquest was, among other things, the execution of a long-deferred sentence upon a people sunk in occult abomination. The LORD is patient, but He is not mocked; the iniquity of the Amorites came to the full, and the city of enchantments fell. The same God still forbids His people every traffic with divination and the dark arts.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

The name is linked to sorcery or enchantment, fitting the dark religion of the Canaanite cities.

expand to see more

Achshaph — Hebrew Akshaph, perhaps “sorcery” or “enchantment.”

The root is akin to words for the practice of witchcraft.

Its king joined the northern league against Israel.

The city lay within the borders of Asher.

The city of enchantment could not enchant away the judgment of God.

Usage

"Like Achshaph, the strongholds of sorcery fall when the LORD executes His righteous sentence."

"Achshaph teaches that no enchantment can turn aside the oath God swore to give the land."

"The city of spells is a warning that God forbids and judges every traffic with the dark arts."
